labctl.notes: HOST-NATIVE (de-bridged): VICE runs on the host, headless, no QEMU/QMP, no guest OS, no X, no exec channel. Frames VICE_SHM_PATH->shm (the same IFB1 wire format drawshm uses), keys vicectl + the shared us-layout keysym table, audio -sounddev wav -> FIFO. Launcher stations/vice-native/x11-runtime.sh; reset=relaunch restores the checkpoint in /data/vms/streamhost/stations/cbm8032/sta/golden.vsf.

render.stationsManifestPrelude: # cbm8032 — host-native VICE 3.10.0 xpet -model 8032 (Commodore CBM 8032, 1980) -> commodore basic 4.0. De-bridged 2026-08-16: no QEMU, no guest, no X (this is the conversion that retired the fleet's only 1600x1200 X root), no ssh. Keyboard-only. Same binary as pet2001, different model.

eraSoftware: Commodore BASIC 4.0, with the PET's disk commands built into the language
WordPro — the word processor that sold 8032s to offices
VisiCalc and Silicon Office on the 8000 series
the 8050 dual floppy and the 4022 tractor printer on the IEEE-488 bus
Waterloo microSystems' languages, from the SuperPET side of the family
museum.blurb: Commodore's office computer: 80 columns of green text, 32 KB, a proper business keyboard, and no colour, no sprites and no sound chip at all. Everything its home-computer siblings are famous for is deliberately missing.
museum.notes: Live streamhost tile. Emulator-in-captured-Linux BRIDGE tile: a captured Debian 13 (trixie) kiosk runs VICE (xpet -model 8032) emulating a CBM 8032; streamhost captures the Linux framebuffer + AC97 audio exactly like every other tile. VICE bundles the Commodore ROMs, so this tile needs no external media — BASIC 4.0, KERNAL 4, the 80-column business editor and the character generator all come from the emulator's own data tree. The golden is the machine's own untouched power-on screen; the exhibit's interaction is the registry demoProgram, a BASIC 4.0 times table that fills all 80 columns. Drawn double-size (-CRTCdsize) on a 1600x1200 X root, the tightest advertised mode that contains the 1408x1064 SDL window. Keyboard-only exhibit; mono-terminal archetype — the 8032 is an all-in-one with an integrated 12-inch green monitor, which is what that archetype models. See streamhost/docs/BRIDGE.md and docs/guests/cbm8032.md.

reset.fixture: Commodore CBM 8032 power-on screen (*** commodore basic 4.0 ***, 31743 bytes free, ready.), HOST-NATIVE: VICE 3.10.0's xpet -model 8032 runs on the host, headless, and publishes the emulated screen straight into the shm mapping at 1408x1088 (-CRTCdsize; there is no -CRTCborders, VICE's CRTC video code has none and asking for it is a hard parse error). That surface REPLACES the bridged tile's 1600x1200 capture, which existed only to contain VICE's fixed SDL window and encoded a black margin around it — this conversion retired the fleet's only 1600x1200 X root. resetMode=relaunch, and this station COLD-BOOTS: the launcher restarts xpet with VICE_NATIVE_CHECKPOINT=0 and no checkpoint is restored. Measured ON THE LIVE STATION 2026-08-16, restoring this machine's snapshot both CHANGES THE PUBLISHED SURFACE (1408x1088 becomes 1408x1316) and CORRUPTS THE RUNNING BASIC — the restored screen printed "?illegal quantity error in  0" under the ready prompt. Either alone would disqualify it. A cold boot is stable to 120 M cycles, and the exhibit loses nothing because the scene IS an untouched cold boot. Keys resolve through PET/gtk3_buuk_sym.vkm, the BUSINESS-UK keyboard — this station and pet2001 share the xpet binary and share no keyboard at all. Keyboard-only exhibit (no mouse); PET sound -> FIFO.
